titles: Do You Actually Need a Financial Advisor?
5 Things a Financial Advisor Should Actually Do for You
You May Not Need a Financial Advisor. Here's How to Know.
description: You may not need a financial advisor — and that answer comes from someone who runs an advisory firm.

Aaron Christopherson, CFP®, lays out the five things a great advisor should actually be doing for you once you've built real wealth, then gives you a five-question test to decide whether you need one at all.
• Why your portfolio has to change the day your paycheck stops
• Thinking years ahead on taxes instead of one April at a time
• The single decision that can undo 30 years of saving
• Why a good advisor will sometimes tell you to spend more
• Whether your plan still works if your spouse has to run it
